label: Aneuploidy score column scale must be validated
text: PITFALL: The provided aneuploidy column may not be on a standard scale, so treating it as a count of altered arms or comparing means can mislead. Standard aneuploidy scores are either the number of altered chromosome arms (0-39, Taylor 2018) or the fraction of called arms altered (0-1, ASCETS); in data_clinical_sample.txt the first data row shows ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE = 319463.6 next to FGA = 0.0017, which is neither. CHECK: describe the range and distribution of ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE, compute its Spearman correlation with FGA, and independently recompute an arm-level score from data_cna_hg19.seg (segment |seg.mean| > 0.2, arm called altered if >= 70% of covered arm length is altered in one direction, score = altered arms / callable arms). IF FOUND (odd scale or weak agreement): use only rank-based tests, run the subtype comparison on all three metrics (provided score, FGA, recomputed arm score), and base the conclusion on whether they agree in direction rather than on one column. SOURCE: https://github.com/beroukhim-lab/ascets ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8388019/ ; https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(18)30111-9

label: Tumor purity confounds FGA and aneuploidy comparisons
text: PITFALL: Low tumor purity compresses copy-number log-ratios toward zero (observed log2 ratio is about log2(purity*CN/2 + 1 - purity), so a one-copy gain at 10% purity gives ~0.07, below the usual 0.1-0.2 calling thresholds), producing falsely 'flat' genomes and low FGA/aneuploidy. Mucinous, low-cellularity tumors are especially affected, so a subtype difference in aneuploidy can be a purity or histology artifact. CHECK: compare TUMOR_PURITY across MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE groups (Kruskal-Wallis), and correlate purity with FGA and ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE (Spearman); count samples with purity <= 20% or missing per subtype. IF FOUND (purity differs by subtype or correlates with the aneuploidy metric): repeat the subtype comparison adjusted for purity (rank-transformed outcome regressed on subtype + purity, or stratified van Elteren/within purity strata) and as a sensitivity restricted to samples with purity >= 20-30%; report whether the TP53-subtype effect survives. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5027494/ ; https://modernpathology.org/article/S0893-3952(22)00261-7/fulltext ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6697733/

label: Test the TP53-subtype contrast, not only the omnibus
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about one specific subtype (the TP53-mut predominant level of MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE) relative to the others, but an omnibus Kruskal-Wallis or k-group log-rank test only says 'some group differs' and can be significant because of a different subtype; conversely re-deriving groups from TP53 mutation status in data_mutations.txt tests a different exposure than the study's cluster label. CHECK: tabulate MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE levels and n per level; run the targeted contrasts (TP53-mut predominant vs all others pooled, and vs each other subtype) and confirm the direction (higher aneuploidy, shorter OS) for each. IF FOUND (more than two subtypes): report the pre-specified TP53-vs-rest contrast as primary, use Dunn's test or Holm-adjusted pairwise tests after Kruskal-Wallis and Holm-adjusted pairwise log-rank for the pairwise view, and do not label the hypothesis from the omnibus p-value alone. SOURCE: https://alexisdinno.com/files/Dinno2014b.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4728021/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3775959/

label: Left truncation: OS from metastasis but entry at sequencing
text: PITFALL: Left truncation (delayed entry / immortal time). OS_MONTHS is measured from metastasis diagnosis, but patients enter the cohort only when their tumor was sequenced, which can be months or years later; patients who died before sequencing are absent, so naive Kaplan-Meier overestimates survival and subtype comparisons are biased if time-to-sequencing differs by subtype. CHECK: compute entry delay = (AGE_AT_SEQUENCING - AGE_AT_METS) * 12 months per patient (only whole-year precision), check for negative values or delay > OS_MONTHS, and compare the delay across MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE groups. IF FOUND (non-trivial delays, or delays differing by subtype): add a sensitivity analysis with risk-set adjustment, i.e. a Cox model / KM with counting-process (entry, exit, event) format (lifelines entry_col, or R Surv(entry, time, status)), dropping or flooring rows where entry >= exit; state whether the subtype hazard ratio keeps its direction and significance. Because entry is year-rounded, treat this as a robustness check and keep the naive analysis as primary. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9190030/ ; https://aacrjournals.org/cebp/article/31/6/1195/699227/Accounting-for-Delayed-Entry-in-Analyses-of ; https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2766816

label: Few events per subtype make survival estimates unstable
text: PITFALL: Survival power depends on the number of deaths, not patients; a small molecular subtype with few events gives unstable hazard ratios, and with zero events in a group Cox estimates diverge (monotone likelihood). A non-significant p-value in a small group is then not evidence against poor prognosis, and a significant one may rest on a handful of deaths. CHECK: tabulate patients and deaths per MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE; report median OS with 95% CI per group and the hazard ratio with 95% CI for TP53-mut predominant vs others, not just the log-rank p; check proportional hazards (Schoenfeld test, look for crossing KM curves). IF FOUND (fewer than ~10 deaths in a group, or zero-event group): use Firth-penalized Cox or exact/permutation log-rank, pool sparse subtypes for the TP53-vs-rest contrast, and if curves cross add a restricted-mean-survival-time comparison; judge the claim on effect direction and CI width as well as the p-value. SOURCE: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.0006-341X.2001.00114.x ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7941573/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8802494/

label: Subtype prognosis is confounded with grade and histology
text: PITFALL: Molecular subtype is entangled with standard prognostic factors (HISTOLOGY, DIFFERENTIATION/grade, STAGE, PCI, treatment), so a crude survival or aneuploidy difference may only reflect, for example, high-grade non-mucinous histology clustering in one subtype. But over-adjusting answers a different question: the hypothesis says 'associated with', which is a marginal claim. CHECK: cross-tabulate MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE against HISTOLOGY, DIFFERENTIATION and STAGE (Fisher/chi-square); fit a multivariable Cox with subtype plus grade/histology and age, keeping the model within about 10 deaths per coefficient. IF FOUND (strong subtype-grade/histology association): keep the unadjusted contrast as the primary test of the stated hypothesis, report the adjusted hazard ratio as a sensitivity result, and say explicitly whether the association is independent of grade or explained by it; do not flip the label solely because adjustment attenuates the effect. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3362085/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6093349/

label: Patient vs sample level and OS_STATUS coding
text: PITFALL: Unit-of-analysis and coding errors when joining cBioPortal-style tables. MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE and OS are patient-level, aneuploidy/FGA/purity are sample-level, and sample IDs with T02/T04 suffixes show some patients may have more than one or a non-first sample; counting a patient twice inflates n and breaks independence. OS_STATUS is a string like '0:LIVING' / '1:DECEASED', missing values are the literal 'NA', and four '#' metadata lines precede the header. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID after the merge, count missing MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE, OS_MONTHS, FGA and ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE, and confirm the event indicator is parsed from the leading digit of OS_STATUS (verify deaths count is plausible). IF FOUND: keep one sample per patient (or average within patient) for aneuploidy tests, run survival strictly at patient level, drop rather than impute missing subtype, and report the n actually used for each test. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3071962/

label: Use seg/FGA with rank tests, not the gene-level CNA matrix
text: PITFALL: Using the wrong table or wrong statistics for aneuploidy. data_cna.txt holds discrete gene-level calls from a targeted panel (mostly 0, with -2/2 for deep deletions and amplifications), which measure focal events, not arm-level aneuploidy; and FGA from panel data is right-skewed with many zeros or near-zeros (cBioPortal FGA = summed length of segments with |seg.mean| above a threshold of about 0.1-0.2 divided by total segment length), so t-tests/ANOVA on raw values are unreliable. CHECK: plot FGA and ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE distributions per subtype, note the share of zeros, and confirm FGA can be reproduced from data_cna_hg19.seg. IF FOUND (skew/zero-inflation): use Mann-Whitney / Kruskal-Wallis with medians and IQRs (optionally compare the proportion of samples above a cutoff with Fisher's exact test), take aneuploidy from the sample table and the .seg file, and do not count altered genes in data_cna.txt as an aneuploidy measure. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/SqtGhn-AZ4s ; https://www.biostars.org/p/406584/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8388019/

label: Hypothesis has two parts; test both separately
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a conjunction of two claims (TP53-mut predominant subtype has higher aneuploidy AND poorer prognosis); supporting one half and silently skipping or stretching the other gives a wrong label, as does calling it 'Not verifiable' when the needed variables exist (MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE, ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE/FGA plus the .seg file, OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS are all present in the clinical tables). CHECK: test each half separately with its own effect size, direction and p-value, and write both results down before choosing a label. IF FOUND (the halves disagree): say so explicitly in the reasoning and decide the label on whether both directional claims hold, instead of averaging the evidence or reporting only the stronger half. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3362085/

label: Denominator: samples without mutation rows are wild-type, not missing
text: PITFALL: In cBioPortal-format studies the mutation file (data_mutations.txt) has one row per mutation, so a sequenced sample with no mutation in the gene of interest (or no mutations at all) simply has no row; building group sizes from the mutation file undercounts wild-type samples and inflates mutation frequency. CHECK: take the denominator from data_clinical_sample.txt joined to data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (here all 32 samples are listed with panel WXS, i.e. whole exome, and the 32 sample IDs match between the two files), and compare with the set of Tumor_Sample_Barcode values in the mutation file. IF FOUND: code every profiled sample absent from the gene's rows as wild-type (0), not as missing, and state n per tumour type from the clinical table. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000 and https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067

label: Define 'mutated' by protein-altering Variant_Classification only
text: PITFALL: This study's data_mutations.txt is not restricted to protein-altering variants (its first rows are Variant_Classification=Intron), so counting any row for a gene as 'mutated' can count silent, intronic, UTR or flanking variants as hits. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification and Consequence for the rows of the gene of interest and for the whole file. IF FOUND: define 'mutated' using only protein-altering classes (Missense_Mutation, Nonsense_Mutation, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Nonstop_Mutation, Translation_Start_Site), which is the maftools default vc_nonSyn set, and report as a sensitivity analysis whether the conclusion changes when all rows are counted. Also match the gene by exact Hugo_Symbol (Entrez_Gene_Id is empty and the file uses old symbols such as C19orf61, so do not join on Entrez ID). SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/maftools/inst/doc/maftools.html and https://github.com/PoisonAlien/maftools/issues/610

label: Unit of analysis is the tumour/patient, not the mutation row
text: PITFALL: A gene can carry two or more mutations in the same sample (maftools calls this Multi_Hit), and a patient can contribute more than one sample; counting mutation rows instead of mutated tumours inflates the count and breaks the independence assumed by exact tests. CHECK: for the gene of interest, count distinct Tumor_Sample_Barcode values rather than rows, and check whether SAMPLE_ID to PATIENT_ID is one-to-one in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: collapse to one binary mutated/wild-type value per patient before building the contingency table. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/maftools/inst/doc/maftools.html

label: Two meanings of 'significantly associated': between-group enrichment vs excess over background rate
text: PITFALL: 'Gene X is significantly associated with tumour types A and B' can be tested two different ways that can disagree in a small exome cohort: (1) between-group enrichment, mutated vs wild-type in A+B against the other tumour types in the study (2x2 exact test), and (2) gene-level significance, whether the number of non-silent mutations in the gene within A and B exceeds what the background (passenger) mutation rate predicts for a gene of that coding length (binomial/Poisson test, the standard 'significantly mutated gene' logic of discovery-screen studies). Test (1) has very low power with a handful of tumours per type; test (2) can be decisive with few tumours because the per-gene background probability is tiny. CHECK: compute both; for (2) estimate the background rate from the study itself (total non-silent somatic mutations in those tumours divided by roughly 30 Mb of coding sequence per exome, or use TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in the sample table) and compute P(at least k mutated tumours of n) for the gene. IF FOUND that the two disagree: say so explicitly and decide the label on the reading that matches the hypothesis wording, rather than reporting only the test that came out non-significant or only the one that came out significant. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2820387/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4048962/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3018819/

label: Fisher's exact test is conservative in small groups; check mid-p/Barnard and sidedness
text: PITFALL: With small groups, Fisher's exact test is conservative (actual type I error well below nominal) and discrete, so a p-value just above 0.05 may reflect the test, not the data, and chi-squared is invalid when expected counts are below 5. Sidedness also matters: a directional hypothesis (mutations enriched in the named types) justifies a one-sided test, but choosing sidedness after seeing the p-value is not legitimate. CHECK: before testing, write down the group sizes and compute the smallest p-value the table margins can produce; then run Fisher two-sided and one-sided, plus Fisher mid-p or an unconditional exact test (scipy.stats.barnard_exact or boschloo_exact). IF FOUND that the verdict flips between Fisher and mid-p/Barnard/Boschloo or between one- and two-sided: report all of them, state which was pre-specified, and treat the result as borderline rather than as a clean positive or negative. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.3531 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4388855/

label: Conjunction claim: test each named tumour type as well as the pooled group
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis names two tumour types jointly (IPMNs and MCNs). Pooling them into one group can give a significant result driven by only one type, while testing each type separately halves the sample and loses power; and the choice of comparator (all other cyst types pooled vs each separately) changes the p-value. CHECK: build the full tumour-type by mutated/wild-type table from CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED / ONCOTREE_CODE (r x 2), run an exact r x 2 test (Fisher-Freeman-Halton), then the pooled named-types vs rest 2x2, then each named type vs the remaining types separately, with a multiplicity note. IF FOUND that mutations occur in only one of the two named types: do not claim support for both from the pooled test; a claim that needs both parts to hold requires evidence in each. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1713204/ and https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMsr077003

label: Zero cells: use exact intervals; 0 of n is not proof of absence
text: PITFALL: A zero cell (for example no mutated tumours in the comparator types) makes the sample odds ratio infinite or zero and makes large-sample confidence intervals meaningless; and zero events in a small group does not show the true rate is zero (the 95% upper bound for 0 of n is about 3/n, e.g. roughly 31-37% for n=8). CHECK: look for any zero or one count in the contingency table. IF FOUND: report per-group proportions with Clopper-Pearson exact intervals and an exact (conditional) odds-ratio interval or a 0.5-corrected odds ratio, and do not describe the comparator types as 'never mutated' or treat a non-significant p as evidence of no association. SOURCE: https://alanagresti.com/articles/agresti_2003.pdf and https://people.stat.sc.edu/hansont/stat770/Chapter3a.pdf

label: Mutation pattern (truncating fraction) is evidence beyond frequency
text: PITFALL: Frequency alone is a weak guide to whether a gene's mutations are selected in a tumour type when the cohort is small; for tumour suppressors the pattern of mutations is the standard second line of evidence (the '20/20 rule': more than 20% of a gene's mutations being inactivating - nonsense, frameshift, splice-site - marks a tumour suppressor, since truncating mutations are a small share of passenger mutations). CHECK: for the gene of interest, tabulate Variant_Classification by tumour type and compare its truncating fraction with the truncating fraction of all other non-silent mutations in the same tumours (exact binomial test). IF FOUND that the gene's mutations are predominantly truncating: treat this as supporting evidence that the mutations are selected rather than passengers, reported alongside (not instead of) the frequency test. SOURCE: https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.1616440113 and https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-pathol-012414-040312

label: Multiplicity: one named gene vs exome-wide scan
text: PITFALL: A gene that is singled out because it looked striking in an exome-wide screen carries selection bias, and if the analyst scans many genes to see which associate with tumour type, uncorrected p-values overstate significance. Conversely, a single pre-named gene needs no genome-wide correction. CHECK: decide whether the analysis tests only the one gene named in the hypothesis or ranks all genes. IF FOUND that all genes are scanned: apply Benjamini-Hochberg or Bonferroni across the genes tested and report where the named gene ranks; if only the named gene is tested, say so and report the unadjusted p as the primary result, with the genome-wide-corrected background-rate p (multiply by about 20,000 genes) as a stringency check. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2820387/ and https://doi.org/10.1214/10-aoas438

label: No call is not proven wild-type: check allele fraction and depth by tumour type
text: PITFALL: Somatic mutation calls from exome sequencing miss mutations in samples with low neoplastic cellularity or low depth (sensitivity falls sharply for allele fractions near 0.1 at about 30x), so a sample with no called mutation in a gene is 'not detected', not proven wild-type; cystic lesions with much stroma are prone to this, and it biases toward under-counting in whichever tumour type has lower purity. CHECK: compute t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count) and total depth per sample from data_mutations.txt and compare the distributions and the number of calls per sample across tumour types. IF FOUND that one tumour type has systematically lower allele fractions or very few calls: flag the wild-type calls in that type as uncertain and note that the between-type comparison may be biased; do not over-read small differences. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.2514 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6887630/

label: Pitfall 1: no direct splicing readout in DNA-only data
text: PITFALL: The claim is about an effect on RNA splicing, but the study tables appear to hold only whole-exome DNA mutation calls (gene panel matrix lists one profile, 'mutations' = WXS) plus a short clinical table; experts establish a splicing effect by RNA-seq of mutant versus wild-type samples (percent-spliced-in, rMATS-type differential splicing, minigene or CRISPR validation), which a mutation table cannot provide, so an analyst can end up reporting textbook knowledge as if it were a result of this data. CHECK: list every file and column and write down, separately for the two halves of the claim ('RNA splicing' and 'haematopoiesis'), which column is a direct readout (expression/isoform/PSI, blood counts, blasts, dysplasia) and which is only indirect (which genes are mutated, mutation pattern, WHO class). IF FOUND (no direct readout): do not state that a splicing change was measured; say explicitly that any evidence is indirect, base the label only on what the tables themselves show, and remember the hypothesis is a joint claim (no effect on splicing AND no effect on haematopoiesis), so each half must be assessed on its own evidence. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-06063-x ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6172604/

label: Pitfall 2: splice-site variant class is not splicing-factor gene
text: PITFALL: Confusing 'splice-site mutations' with 'mutations in splicing machinery genes'. Variant_Classification values such as Splice_Site or Splice_Region are cis mutations at an intron/exon boundary of any gene; the hypothesis concerns trans-acting mutations in genes that encode spliceosome components. Filtering on Variant_Classification answers a different question. CHECK: define the exposure by Hugo_Symbol against a pre-specified spliceosome gene list (core 3' splice-site recognition factors such as SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, ZRSR2, SF3A1, SF1, U2AF2, PRPF40B, plus a broader list such as KEGG spliceosome), never by Variant_Classification or Consequence. IF FOUND: redo the exposure definition by gene; keep cis splice-site variants in other genes out of the 'splicing machinery mutated' group. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5418633/

label: Pitfall 3: gene symbol aliases hide splicing genes
text: PITFALL: Splicing-factor genes are missed because of old or alias gene symbols and symbol corruption: U2AF35 = U2AF1, U2AF65 = U2AF2, SFRS2/SC35 = SRSF2, U2AF1RS2/URP = ZRSR2, SF3B155/SAP155 = SF3B1; spreadsheets also turn symbols such as SEPT/MARCH genes into dates. The Entrez_Gene_Id column in data_mutations.txt looks empty, so symbols are the only key. CHECK: list all unique Hugo_Symbol values, match them case-insensitively against both current and alias symbols for the spliceosome gene list, and scan for date-like or malformed symbols. IF FOUND: map aliases to the current HGNC symbol before counting mutated patients; report the gene list actually used. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7856679/ ; https://www.omim.org/entry/191317

label: Pitfall 4: pathway recurrence needs a background model
text: PITFALL: Treating 'several patients carry a mutation in some splicing gene' as proof of selection. A spliceosome gene set contains 100+ genes and a lot of coding sequence, so with a few hundred somatic mutations in a ~29-exome cohort some hits are expected by chance; choosing the gene set after looking at the mutation list, counting mutations instead of patients, and ignoring gene length and background mutation rate all inflate the signal. CHECK: fix the gene set before looking; compute the expected number of nonsilent hits in the set from the cohort's total mutation count and the set's share of exome coding length (Poisson/binomial), compare with the observed count, count each patient once, and compare nonsilent with silent mutations in the set. IF FOUND (observed is not clearly above expectation, or the result depends on a post-hoc list): report recurrence as descriptive only and do not call the pathway 'significantly mutated'. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12213 ; https://www.sanger.ac.uk/tool/dndscv/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9179938/

label: Pitfall 5: hotspot vs truncating pattern is indirect evidence
text: PITFALL: Reading function straight off a mutation list. The mutation pattern in a gene (same codon hit repeatedly by missense or in-frame changes = hotspot/altered-function pattern; scattered frameshift/nonsense/splice-site = loss-of-function pattern) is the accepted indirect evidence that mutations are selected and functional, but it shows selection, not which molecular process (splicing) changes. CHECK: for each splicing-factor gene tabulate Protein_position / HGVSp_Short / Variant_Classification per patient and the Hotspot column; note whether hits cluster at one residue, whether any are silent, and whether truncating variants occur. IF FOUND (clustered hotspot or consistent truncating pattern): describe it as indirect evidence that the mutations are non-random and functionally selected, and state that the consequence for splicing is inferred, not measured; if hits are scattered single missense variants, treat them as possible passengers. SOURCE: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2211124718301529 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6029450/

label: Pitfall 6: mutual exclusivity tests are miscalibrated and underpowered
text: PITFALL: Testing mutual exclusivity (or co-occurrence) of splicing-factor mutations with a plain Fisher's exact test. Fisher assumes every tumour has the same chance of carrying each mutation; when mutation load or disease subtype differs between samples it gives spurious co-occurrence and misses real exclusivity, and in a cohort of about 29 patients exclusivity between genes each mutated in a handful of patients is almost never statistically detectable. CHECK: tabulate per-sample mutation counts (TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS) and WHO class; build the patient-by-gene 0/1 matrix for the splicing genes; if testing, use a permutation that preserves per-sample and per-gene totals (DISCOVER-style null) and report how many patients carry 0, 1, or 2+ splicing-gene mutations. IF FOUND (load or subtype varies, or n is tiny): present exclusivity as a descriptive count, do not claim significance from Fisher, and do not read a non-significant result as 'no exclusivity'. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5162102/ ; https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(19)30503-3

label: Pitfall 7: non-significance in a small cohort is not support for no effect
text: PITFALL: Concluding the null hypothesis is supported ('True') because a mutant-versus-wild-type comparison gave p > 0.05. With roughly 29 patients, absence of a significant difference is absence of evidence, not evidence of no effect; a no-effect claim needs an equivalence-type argument (confidence interval lying inside a pre-set smallest effect of interest). CHECK: for every comparison report the effect size with an exact confidence interval and the group sizes; ask what effect the sample could have detected. IF FOUND (wide interval that includes both zero and large effects): do not use the result as support for the hypothesis; the comparison is uninformative and the label must rest on other evidence or on the absence of relevant variables. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5502906/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12567074/

label: Pitfall 8: case-only cohort, haematopoiesis only via WHO class
text: PITFALL: The cohort is case-only: every patient already has a myeloid neoplasm (MDS and related diagnoses), so there is no unaffected comparison group and 'does the mutation affect haematopoiesis' cannot be tested as diseased-versus-healthy. The only haematopoiesis-related variables look like WHO_CLASS, CYTOGENETICS and IPSS_SCORE in data_clinical_patient.txt; WHO class encodes a marrow phenotype (for example ring sideroblasts, excess blasts, monocytosis) but it is a diagnostic category, and associations inside a diseased cohort are conditioned on disease (collider/selection bias) and confounded by subtype mix (sample IDs suggest MDS and tAML cases are pooled). CHECK: cross-tabulate splicing-gene mutation status (per gene and pooled) against WHO_CLASS, IPSS and karyotype with exact tests and report the table itself; check whether any blood-count, blast or dysplasia column exists. IF FOUND (only class-level phenotype available): describe any link as an association between mutation and disease subtype within patients, not a causal effect on haematopoiesis, and say plainly whether the tables contain a direct haematopoiesis measure. SOURCE: https://academic.oup.com/ije/article/47/1/226/4259077 ; https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1103283

label: Pitfall 9: unit of analysis and denominator in MAF data
text: PITFALL: Wrong unit and wrong denominator. A MAF lists only mutated genes, so samples with no call are absent from it; and the patient table appears to have one row fewer than the sample table, so a patient may have two samples. Counting mutation rows, or using only samples present in the MAF, distorts every frequency and test. CHECK: take the denominator from data_clinical_sample.txt / data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (all WXS-profiled samples), compare the set of Tumor_Sample_Barcode values with SAMPLE_ID, count samples per PATIENT_ID, and look for duplicated rows of the same variant in the same sample. IF FOUND: analyse one record per patient (mutated if any sample is mutated), treat profiled samples missing from the MAF as wild-type, and de-duplicate variants before counting. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (general format documentation, cited from prior knowledge and not retrieved in this session)

label: Pitfall 10: wild-type calls are lower bounds; no allele counts
text: PITFALL: 'Wild-type' means 'no mutation detected', not 'no mutation'. The germline control here is CD3+ T cells; in myeloid neoplasms T-cell fractions can contain clonal myeloid DNA, which makes somatic callers drop real mutations, and exome capture covers some regions unevenly, so splicing-gene status is misclassified in some patients and associations are biased toward no difference. The t_ref_count / t_alt_count columns also look empty, so allele fraction, clonality and heterozygosity cannot be computed. CHECK: confirm whether the read-count columns are populated; check GERMLINE_CONTROL and SOMATIC_STATUS per sample; check Validation_Status. IF FOUND (no counts, T-cell control): do not make claims about heterozygosity, clone size or order of mutations, and state that mutation frequencies are lower bounds. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5969383/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12672828/

label: The alteration in the claim (a rearrangement) is a structural variant, and a MAF cannot hold one
text: PITFALL: A MAF mutation table (data_mutations.txt) records only small variants (Variant_Type SNP/DNP/TNP/ONP/INS/DEL); in cBioPortal-style studies rearrangements/translocations live in a separate structural-variant table (data_sv.txt with Site1_Hugo_Symbol/Site2_Hugo_Symbol/Class), and no such table is among the three files given, so a gene's 'rearrangement status' may simply not be a variable in the data. CHECK: List every file and every column; tabulate Variant_Type and Variant_Classification in data_mutations.txt; search all column names and all clinical values for any SV/fusion/translocation/rearrangement field or a per-sample TERT-status field (the clinical sample header shows only MYCN_AMP, PURITY, PLOIDY, coverage and TMB columns). IF FOUND: If no table or column encodes rearrangements, treat TERT-rearrangement status as unmeasured rather than building it from MAF rows; the label must then follow the task rubric for a missing variable, not a statistical test on a stand-in. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Encyclopedia/pages/Variant_Type/ ; https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/.

label: Proxy substitution: TERT point mutations (or any TERT row in the MAF) are not TERT rearrangements
text: PITFALL: Analysts grep the MAF for Hugo_Symbol == TERT and call carriers 'TERT-altered', but neuroblastoma TERT rearrangements are breakpoints in non-coding DNA around/upstream of the TERT locus at 5p15.33 that juxtapose enhancers (enhancer hijacking) and are found by whole-genome sequencing or break-apart FISH, not as coding SNVs/indels; a coding TERT SNV is a different event with different biology. CHECK: If any MAF rows have Hugo_Symbol TERT (or lie in chr5:~1.25-1.35 Mb), print their Variant_Classification, Variant_Type, positions and HGVSp: missense/silent/indel rows are small variants, not rearrangements. IF FOUND: Do not use TERT SNV/indel carriers (or TERT expression, MYCN status, TMB or any other column) as a surrogate for rearrangement status; say explicitly that the rearrangement variable is absent and that any result on TERT point mutations does not test the stated hypothesis. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556277/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10147-020-01773-z ; https://aacrjournals.org/cancerrescommun/article-split/5/1/167/751301/Serially-Quantifying-TERT-Rearrangement ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-13885-w.

label: Absence of TERT rows in a capture-based MAF is not evidence that no tumour has a TERT rearrangement
text: PITFALL: The sample table has MEAN_TARGET_COVERAGE columns, i.e. target-capture (exome-like) sequencing; exome data detect only the minority of rearrangements whose breakpoints fall in or near exons, lack coverage of intergenic/promoter DNA, and the GC-rich TERT upstream region is notoriously poorly captured, so 'zero TERT events in the MAF' reflects the assay, not the tumours. CHECK: Tabulate Variant_Classification: if rows are almost all coding/splice (few or no IGR, 5'Flank, Intron) the call set is exome-restricted; confirm there are no calls in the non-coding 5p15.33 region. IF FOUND: Never score samples without TERT rows as 'TERT-rearrangement negative' and never conclude 'no low-risk tumour carries a rearrangement' from the MAF; the negative class is unobserved, so frequency, subgroup and outcome comparisons on it are invalid. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/ajhg/fulltext/S0002-9297(16)30052-0 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gim.2022.09.017 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8756133/ ; https://doi.org/10.18632/oncotarget.6171.

label: 'Poor outcomes' needs an observed outcome variable (event status and follow-up time); check that one exists
text: PITFALL: A prognostic claim can only be tested with survival/event data (in cBioPortal clinical files: OS_STATUS/OS_MONTHS, EFS/DFS/PFS status and months, relapse, vital status); the patient table header here shows only PATIENT_ID, STAGE, AGE_IN_DAYS, RISK_GROUP and the sample table only assay/tumour descriptors, so an outcome may be entirely absent. CHECK: Enumerate all columns of data_clinical_patient.txt and data_clinical_sample.txt (including the '#' description lines) and look for any death/event/relapse/progression/follow-up-time field. IF FOUND: If none exists, the outcome half of the claim has no variable: do not run a test on a substitute and do not report a 'no difference' result as contradiction; state that outcome is unmeasured and apply the task rubric for missing variables. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1001216.

label: Risk group, stage, age and MYCN status are baseline stratifiers, not outcomes (circularity)
text: PITFALL: Neuroblastoma risk group (INRG/COG low/intermediate/high) is a pre-treatment classification computed from age at diagnosis (18-month cut-off, about 547 days), stage, MYCN amplification and other biology; using RISK_GROUP or STAGE as a stand-in for 'poor outcome' is circular, and within the 'low-risk' stratum named in the hypothesis RISK_GROUP is constant so it cannot measure outcome at all. CHECK: Print the distinct values of RISK_GROUP and STAGE (note coding such as HR/IR/LR, 4 vs 4S, missing values) and cross-tabulate RISK_GROUP against STAGE, AGE_IN_DAYS >= 547 and MYCN_AMP to confirm it is derived from them. IF FOUND: Use RISK_GROUP only to define the stratum the hypothesis is about (low-risk; do not lump intermediate-risk or missing into it); never interpret an association between an alteration and risk group/stage/age as an association with outcome. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2650388/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8500606/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5918153/.

label: Compound claim: every component must map to a variable, and the label must come from the data, not from recalled literature
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis has three parts: (a) TERT-rearrangement status, (b) restriction to the low-risk group, (c) worse outcome; being able to measure one part (e.g. risk group exists) does not make the claim testable, and analysts who recognise the topic tend to label from memory of published neuroblastoma findings (reviews discuss TERT rearrangements, MYCN amplification and ATRX loss as telomere-maintenance routes in the context of risk groups) instead of from the tables. CHECK: Before any modelling, write a three-row map: component -> exact file and column that measures it -> number of non-missing values; mark any component with no column. IF FOUND: Decide the label strictly by the task rubric: 'False' requires that the relevant variables are identified in the data and their analysis contradicts the claim; 'Not verifiable' applies when the data hold no relevant variables; background knowledge may explain a result but must not be the evidence for the label, and the reasoning should name which components were and were not measurable. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1001216 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7313726/ ; https://www.ejcped.com/article/S2772-610X(24)00015-1/fulltext.

label: File parsing and denominators: MAF starts with a '#sequenced_samples' line; missing from MAF is wild-type only if profiled
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt begins with a comment line '#sequenced_samples: ...' so the real header is line 2 (a naive read gives one garbage column), and in cBioPortal data a sample with no MAF rows is 'profiled, no mutation' only if it is in the sequenced list; sample IDs here are non-contiguous (e.g. the list skips some NBL numbers), so clinical and sequenced sets may differ. CHECK: Read the MAF with comment='#' (and the clinical tables skipping '#' lines); compare three ID sets: SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt, the #sequenced_samples list, and unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode; check one sample per patient. IF FOUND: Use the sequenced list as the denominator for any mutation frequency, code unprofiled samples as NA not wild-type, and report n per risk group after the join rather than assuming 56. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000.

label: Confounding and wrong comparison group: the alteration must be compared within the low-risk stratum
text: PITFALL: In neuroblastoma MYCN amplification, TERT rearrangement and ATRX loss are nearly mutually exclusive telomere-maintenance routes that track with risk group, age and stage, so a pooled 'altered vs all others' comparison across risk groups measures the risk-group mix (Simpson-type bias), and the answer changes with the reference group (other low-risk tumours vs MYCN-amplified vs all). CHECK: Cross-tabulate any alteration indicator used against RISK_GROUP and MYCN_AMP and report the count of alteration-positive patients inside the low-risk group specifically. IF FOUND: Restrict the outcome comparison to low-risk patients (alteration-positive vs alteration-negative low-risk); if there are zero or one positives in that stratum the within-stratum effect is not estimable, which is 'cannot settle', not contradiction. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7313726/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4122484/ ; https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1001216.

label: Tiny subgroup and few events: asymptotic log-rank/Cox mislead, and non-significance is not evidence against
text: PITFALL: With about 56 patients, a low-risk subset far smaller and events rare in low-risk disease, asymptotic log-rank and Cox tests are unreliable, Cox estimates diverge when events occur in only one group (monotone likelihood), a Fisher test on event yes/no ignores censoring, and a non-significant p-value from an underpowered comparison gets misread as contradicting the hypothesis. CHECK: Only if both an alteration variable and an outcome variable really exist: tabulate patients and events per group within low-risk before testing. IF FOUND: With any cell <5 or zero events in a group use exact/permutation log-rank or Firth-penalised Cox, report counts and a confidence interval, and treat a wide interval as inconclusive rather than as support or contradiction. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2950789/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4673318/ ; https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1001216.

reason: Determines the overall structure of the analysis and the label rule: both halves must be tested, and the choice between a tested label and 'Not verifiable' depends on whether these columns exist.
text: The hypothesis is a conjunction of two directional claims: the TP53-mut predominant subtype has (1) higher tumour aneuploidy AND (2) poorer prognosis. The library reports that columns for every part appear to be present in the clinical tables (MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE; ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE and FGA, plus the segment file data_cna_hg19.seg; OS_MONTHS and OS_STATUS) - confirm this yourself by listing the columns before choosing between a tested label and 'Not verifiable'. Test each half separately, and write down the effect size, direction and p-value for both halves before choosing a label. If the halves disagree, say so explicitly and decide on whether both directional claims hold; do not average the evidence or report only the stronger half.

reason: Fixes which grouping variable and which contrast answer the hypothesis; using the omnibus test or a re-derived TP53 status would test a different question.
text: The exposure is the study's own cluster label (the 'TP53-mut predominant' level of MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE), not TP53 mutation status re-derived from data_mutations.txt, which would be a different exposure. Tabulate the MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE levels and n per level. If there are more than two subtypes, an omnibus Kruskal-Wallis or k-group log-rank test only shows that some group differs and may be driven by another subtype. Make the pre-specified contrast 'TP53-mut predominant vs all other subtypes pooled' the primary test for both aneuploidy and survival; add pairwise contrasts against each other subtype (Dunn or Holm-adjusted pairwise tests for aneuploidy, Holm-adjusted pairwise log-rank for survival) and check the direction in each. Do not choose the label from an omnibus p-value alone.

reason: The aneuploidy half can be mis-measured in three ways (wrong table, non-standard score scale, parametric tests on zero-inflated data); this tells the team which sources and tests are valid and to cross-check metrics.
text: Take care over how aneuploidy is measured. (a) data_cna.txt holds discrete gene-level calls from a targeted panel (mostly 0, with -2/2 for deep deletions/amplifications); these are focal events, so do not count altered genes there as an aneuploidy measure. Use the sample-table columns and data_cna_hg19.seg. (b) ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE may not be on a standard scale: standard scores are a count of altered chromosome arms (0-39) or a fraction of arms altered (0-1), but the first data row of data_clinical_sample.txt shows ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE = 319463.6 beside FGA = 0.0017. Describe its range and distribution and its Spearman correlation with FGA. (c) Independently recompute an arm-level score from the .seg file (e.g. segments with |seg.mean| > 0.2; an arm is altered if >= 70% of its covered length is altered in one direction; score = altered arms / callable arms) and check that FGA can be reproduced from the .seg file (FGA = length of segments with |seg.mean| above about 0.1-0.2 divided by total segment length). (d) Panel-derived FGA is right-skewed with many zeros or near-zeros, so use rank-based tests (Mann-Whitney / Kruskal-Wallis) with medians and IQRs, optionally Fisher's exact test on the share above a cutoff, not t-tests/ANOVA on raw values. Run the subtype comparison on all three metrics (provided score, FGA, recomputed arm score) and base the aneuploidy conclusion on whether they agree in direction, not on one column.

reason: Purity is a specific, checkable confounder of the aneuploidy comparison that the team would be unlikely to consider from the data alone.
text: Low tumour purity compresses copy-number log-ratios toward zero (observed log2 ratio is about log2(purity*CN/2 + 1 - purity); a one-copy gain at 10% purity gives about 0.07, below the usual 0.1-0.2 calling thresholds), so low-cellularity (e.g. mucinous) tumours can look falsely 'flat' with low FGA/aneuploidy. A subtype difference in aneuploidy can therefore be a purity or histology artefact. Compare TUMOR_PURITY across MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE groups, correlate purity with FGA and ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE (Spearman), and count samples with purity <= 20% or missing per subtype. If purity differs by subtype or correlates with the aneuploidy metric, repeat the subtype comparison adjusted for purity (rank-transformed outcome regressed on subtype + purity, or a stratified test within purity strata) and as a sensitivity analysis restricted to samples with purity >= 20-30%; report whether the TP53-subtype effect survives.

reason: Prevents double-counting patients and mis-parsed event/missing codes, either of which would silently distort both tests.
text: Check the unit of analysis and the coding when joining the tables. MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE and OS are patient-level, while aneuploidy/FGA/purity are sample-level; sample IDs with suffixes such as T02/T04 suggest some patients have more than one sample or a non-first sample. OS_STATUS is a string like '0:LIVING' / '1:DECEASED', missing values are the literal 'NA', and four '#' metadata lines precede the header of the clinical tables. After merging, count samples per PATIENT_ID and count missing MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE, OS_MONTHS, FGA and ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE; parse the event indicator from the leading digit of OS_STATUS and check the death count is plausible. Keep one sample per patient (or average within patient) for aneuploidy tests, run survival strictly at patient level, drop rather than impute missing subtype, and report the n actually used in each test.

reason: Changes which survival methods are valid with few events and how a non-significant or fragile result should be read when choosing the label.
text: Survival power depends on the number of deaths, not patients. Tabulate patients and deaths per MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE. Report median OS with 95% CI per group and the hazard ratio with 95% CI for TP53-mut predominant vs others, not only the log-rank p; check proportional hazards (Schoenfeld test, crossing Kaplan-Meier curves). If a group has fewer than about 10 deaths or zero events (where ordinary Cox estimates diverge), use Firth-penalised Cox or an exact/permutation log-rank test, pool sparse subtypes for the TP53-vs-rest contrast, and add a restricted-mean-survival-time comparison if curves cross. Judge the prognosis half on effect direction and CI width as well as the p-value: a non-significant p in a small group is not by itself evidence against poor prognosis, and a significant one may rest on a handful of deaths.

reason: Sets which estimate (crude vs adjusted) decides the label, avoiding both an unexamined confounded result and an over-adjusted answer to a different question.
text: Molecular subtype is likely entangled with standard prognostic factors (HISTOLOGY, DIFFERENTIATION/grade, STAGE, PCI, treatment). text: Check whether TERT-rearrangement status is actually a variable in the data before using anything as one. The sample table's MEAN_TARGET_COVERAGE columns indicate target-capture (exome-like) sequencing, which misses most such breakpoints and captures the GC-rich TERT upstream region poorly. text: PLAN (bd01-team-a analyst): Quantity: (a) number/fraction of WXS-profiled patients (denominator from sample table + panel matrix, one record per patient) carrying a non-silent somatic mutation in a spliceosome gene set fixed in advance (core: SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, ZRSR2, SF3A1, SF1, U2AF2, PRPF40B, with aliases U2AF35/SFRS2/URP etc; plus a broader pre-specified spliceosome list), versus the Poisson/binomial expectation from the set's share of coding length and the cohort's total non-silent mutation count; (b) within-gene mutation pattern (hotspot codon recurrence vs scattered, silent vs non-silent, truncating); (c) Fisher exact cross-tabs of splicing-mutant status vs WHO class, cytogenetics (normal/abnormal), IPSS, with exact CIs. Checks: column inventory for direct splicing readouts (RNA/PSI) and direct haematopoiesis readouts (counts, blasts); duplicates; sample-vs-patient mapping; alias/date-mangled symbols; read-count columns populated; Splice_Site variant class kept separate from gene-set exposure. Label rule: the two halves judged separately; non-significant small-sample comparisons will not be read as support for no-effect; if no direct splicing/haematopoiesis readout exists, label rests on whether indirect evidence (enrichment + hotspot pattern + subtype association) contradicts the claim or whether variables are simply absent. I would change method if samples per patient >1, duplicates exist, or the gene set result depends on the list chosen.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd02-team-a analyst): Quantity: proportion of tumours (one per patient) with a protein-altering RNF43 mutation, per tumour type (IPMN, MCN, SCA, SPN; n from data_clinical_sample.txt, unmutated = profiled WXS sample with no qualifying RNF43 row). Pre-specified tests on the single named gene RNF43 (no gene scan): (Reading 1) exact r x 2 Fisher-Freeman-Halton across 4 types; pooled IPMN+MCN vs SCA+SPN 2x2 with Fisher two-sided (primary), one-sided, mid-p, Barnard/Boschloo, Clopper-Pearson CIs per group, exact conditional OR CI and 0.5-corrected OR; IPMN alone and MCN alone vs comparators. (Reading 2) binomial/Poisson test of the number of RNF43-mutated IPMN and MCN tumours against the study's own background rate (non-silent mutations per ~30 Mb exome, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS cross-check), assumed RNF43 coding length ~2.35 kb with sensitivity 1-10 kb, plus Bonferroni x20,000; done for IPMN and MCN separately. Supporting: truncating fraction of RNF43 mutations vs other non-silent mutations (20/20 rule). Checks: sample/panel/mutation barcode agreement, SAMPLE-PATIENT one-to-one, Variant_Classification tabulation, multiple RNF43 rows per sample, sensitivity counting all RNF43 rows, minimum attainable p from margins. Change method if: samples not one per patient (collapse), zero cells (exact intervals), mutations in only one of the two named types (report separately, not pooled only), readings disagree (label on reading best matching hypothesis wording and say so).

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd01-team-b): Hypothesis = splicing-machinery gene mutations do not affect RNA splicing or haematopoiesis. Data = 29 myeloid-neoplasm patients (MDS/tAML/CMML), WXS mutations (260 rows), patient/sample clinical tables, panel matrix. Step 1 audit: ID agreement across the 4 files, duplicate mutation rows, TMB vs mutation counts, column fill. Step 2: decide whether any outcome variable measures RNA splicing (expression/exon usage) or haematopoiesis (blood counts, blasts, colony assays) - if none, the claim's outcome side is not directly testable. Step 3: quantify what is testable: frequency of splicing-factor mutations (U2AF1/U2AF35, SRSF2, SF3B1, ZRSR2, SF3A1, SF1, U2AF2, PRPF40B etc), hotspot recurrence, mutual exclusivity, enrichment vs expected by gene length (binomial), association with WHO class/age/sex/IPSS (Fisher exact, small n). Label rule: False only if data contain variables giving evidence of an effect on splicing or haematopoiesis; Not verifiable if only mutation presence is available with no outcome; I would change approach if a splicing/haematological phenotype column exists or if the files mismatch.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd04-team-a analyst): Quantity: whether TERT-rearrangement-positive low-risk neuroblastoma patients have worse outcome than rearrangement-negative low-risk patients. Method: first build a 3-row component map (TERT rearrangement status, low-risk membership, outcome) -> file/column -> non-missing n, by enumerating all columns of the 3 files; if all exist, within-low-risk exact/permutation log-rank with counts. Checks: read MAF with comment='#', compare ID sets (clinical sample, sequenced list, MAF barcodes), one sample per patient; tabulate Variant_Type/Variant_Classification; search for TERT rows / chr5:1.25-1.35Mb and any SV/fusion/outcome column; crosstab RISK_GROUP vs STAGE/age/MYCN. Change of method: if no rearrangement variable or no outcome variable exists, no test on a surrogate is run and the label follows the task rubric for missing variables (Not verifiable).

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd02-team-b): Estimate the association between RNF43 mutation status (sample-level, any non-silent somatic RNF43 mutation in data_mutations.txt) and cyst type (IPMN+MCN vs SCA+SPN, from CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED / sample ID prefix) across the WXS-profiled samples. Method: 2x2 Fisher exact test (one- and two-sided), plus per-type counts (IPMN, MCN, SCA, SPN) and 4-group Fisher/Freeman-Halton. Checks: sample/patient/panel/MAF ID concordance, duplicates in MAF, samples with zero mutations counted as wild-type, silent vs non-silent RNF43 calls, variant classes (truncating?), multiple RNF43 hits per sample collapsed to sample level, gene alias check. Change method if: samples not all profiled (drop unprofiled from denominator), multiple samples per patient (collapse to patient), or RNF43 calls only silent/intronic (exclude).

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd04-team-b): Hypothesis = TERT rearrangements define a subgroup of LOW-risk neuroblastomas with poor outcome. Quantities needed: (a) per-tumour TERT rearrangement status, (b) risk group, (c) an outcome variable (survival/event/status). Method: audit all 3 files (patient n, sample n, ID overlap, duplicates, column lists); search every column and the mutation table for TERT/structural-variant/fusion records and for any survival/outcome field. If TERT-SV status exists, cross-tab against RISK_GROUP (Fisher exact) and, if outcome exists, compare outcome by TERT status within risk groups. Checks: ID match across files, duplicate rows, Variant_Classification/Variant_Type values, any TERT rows and what kind. Change of method: if no rearrangement variable or no outcome variable exists, the claim cannot be tested directly; then decide between False (if the data show TERT status tied to high-risk rather than low-risk) and Not verifiable (if no TERT-rearrangement variable at all).

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: the dataset (56 patients, 56 samples, 920 mutation rows) contains zero TERT records of any kind: no TERT/rearrangement/fusion/SV string in any of the 3 files, no mutation rows on chr5 below 2 Mb, and the mutation table holds only SNP/DEL/INS/DNP small variants. MEANS: TERT rearrangement status per tumour cannot be derived; absence of TERT rows is absence of a structural-variant table, not evidence that no tumour has a rearrangement. ACTION: abandoned the planned TERT-by-risk-group Fisher test; did not treat all samples as TERT-wildtype.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: the clinical tables have no outcome variable at all (patient columns are only STAGE, AGE_IN_DAYS, RISK_GROUP; sample columns are MYCN_AMP, PURITY, PLOIDY, coverage, TMB); no survival, vital status, event or relapse field exists. MEANS: the 'poor outcomes' half of the hypothesis is untestable independently of the TERT half. ACTION: no survival analysis attempted; RISK_GROUP (39 High, 17 Low) is not used as an outcome proxy because it is the stratifier in the claim, not the outcome.

label: RESULT
text: bd04-team-b conclusion: for the hypothesis 'TERT rearrangements define a subgroup of low-risk neuroblastomas with poor outcomes', the provided data (clinical patient/sample tables plus a small-variant MAF, 56 tumours, 39 High / 17 Low risk) hold neither a TERT rearrangement/structural-variant variable nor any outcome variable, so the label chosen is Not verifiable.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE is not on a standard scale: range 0 to 2.16e7 (median 7.7e5), not 0-39 arms or 0-1; 9 samples are exactly 0 while FGA has 52 zeros; Spearman rho with FGA = 0.91 (n=273). MEANS: the column is an unlabelled, heavy-tailed quantity (possibly altered base-pairs or similar), usable only by rank and not interpretable as arm counts. ACTION: used rank-based tests only, and recomputed an independent arm-level score and FGA from data_cna_hg19.seg to base the conclusion on agreement across three metrics.

label: WARNING SIGN

MEANS: survival analysis runs on about 244 patients, not 273; no multi-sample de-duplication is needed. label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: no TERT-rearrangement variable exists in the three given files: the MAF (920 rows, 56 samples) holds only small variants (SNP 818, DEL 48, INS 44, DNP 10; 4 of 920 rows are flank/IGR), has zero rows with Hugo_Symbol TERT and zero rows in chr5:1.0-1.6 Mb, and no SV/fusion table or per-sample TERT column is present. MEANS: rearrangement-positive versus rearrangement-negative cannot be defined for any patient, and absence of TERT rows is an assay limit, not wild-type. ACTION: ran no test on a surrogate (TERT point mutations, MYCN, TMB); treated the exposure component as unmeasured.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: no outcome variable exists: data_clinical_patient.txt has only PATIENT_ID, STAGE, AGE_IN_DAYS, RISK_GROUP and data_clinical_sample.txt only assay/tumour descriptors (MYCN_AMP, PURITY, PLOIDY, coverage, TMB); a keyword search for OS/EFS/relapse/vital status found 0 columns. MEANS: 'poor outcomes' cannot be measured, and RISK_GROUP (17 Low, 39 High; Low = stages 1/2/4S, all MYCN non-amplified) is a pre-treatment classification, constant inside the low-risk stratum. ACTION: did not use RISK_GROUP, STAGE or age as outcome; label follows the rubric for missing variables (Not verifiable).

label: RESULT
text: For the TERT-rearrangement/low-risk/outcome hypothesis, team-a found the ID sets clean (56 patients = 56 samples = 56 sequenced = 56 MAF barcodes, one sample per patient, no duplicate MAF rows), so the ID-mismatch pitfall is absent; of the three hypothesis components only low-risk membership (RISK_GROUP, 56 non-missing, 17 Low) is measurable, so team-a's label is Not verifiable.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: Two RNF43 calls are the same variant p.R371* with very low read support (IPMN_21: 2 alt of 11 reads; MCN_166: 4 alt of 15), and two more have VAF<=0.10 (IPMN_20 0.10, MCN_170 0.07). MEANS: some RNF43 calls may be weak; the mutant count could be inflated, especially in MCN. ACTION: kept the primary sample-level definition (any non-silent RNF43) but re-ran with alt reads>=8 (8/16 vs 0/16, Fisher p=0.0025) and truncating-only AND alt>=8 (6/16 vs 0/16, p=0.018); the association holds in every variant, so method unchanged.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: IPMN+MCN samples carry 3.4x more non-silent mutations than SCA+SPN (312 vs 91), and within IPMN+MCN the RNF43-mutant samples have more mutations (mean 25.6 vs 11.7). MEANS: a gene could look enriched in IPMN/MCN purely from higher mutation burden. ACTION: added a background-rate check: given each sample's burden and RNF43 coding length, the expected number of RNF43-mutant IPMN/MCN samples by chance is 0.024 versus 9 observed (Poisson p~1e-20), and 8 of 10 RNF43 calls are nonsense versus 29 of 440 overall, so burden does not explain it; Fisher test retained as primary.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: In an exome-wide scan of 350 mutated genes for IPMN+MCN vs SCA+SPN, RNF43 (9/16 vs 0/16, Fisher two-sided p=0.0008) ranks second after KRAS but does not pass Bonferroni (0.29) or BH (0.14) across genes; also MCN alone is weak (3/8 vs 0/16, p=0.028; 2/8 p=0.10 after read filter). MEANS: significance depends on treating RNF43 as a pre-specified single hypothesis; the IPMN signal (6/8) drives it. ACTION: no method change, since the hypothesis names RNF43 in advance so a single test is appropriate; reported the MCN weakness as the weakest point.

label: RESULT
text: bd02 result (team-b): In the 32-sample pancreatic cyst WXS study (8 each IPMN, MCN, SCA, SPN; one sample per patient, all WXS-profiled), non-silent RNF43 mutations occur in 6/8 IPMN, 3/8 MCN, 0/8 SCA, 0/8 SPN; IPMN+MCN vs SCA+SPN Fisher two-sided p=0.0008, robust to read-depth and truncating-only filters (p<=0.018). Label chosen: True.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: RNF43 contingency table has zero cells: protein-altering RNF43 mutations in 6/8 IPMN, 3/8 MCN, 0/8 SCA, 0/8 SPN (32 WXS tumours, one per patient), so the sample odds ratio is infinite. MEANS: Wald intervals and chi-squared are invalid, and 0/8 only bounds the comparator rate below 37% (Clopper-Pearson). ACTION: used exact tests only (Fisher-Freeman-Halton 4x2 p=0.00099; pooled IPMN+MCN vs SCA+SPN Fisher two-sided p=0.00082, Boschloo 0.00030), exact conditional OR lower bound 3.18 and 0.5-corrected OR 41.8; did not call SCA/SPN never mutated.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: RNF43 mutations are uneven across the two named types: IPMN 6/8 (75%) vs MCN 3/8 (37.5%). IPMN alone vs SCA+SPN is Fisher p=0.0002, but MCN alone vs SCA+SPN is Fisher two-sided p=0.028 (mid-p 0.014, Boschloo 0.020, Barnard 0.051; smallest attainable Fisher p for these margins is 0.028), and MCN vs all other types including IPMN is p=0.65. MEANS: the pooled result is driven mostly by IPMN; the MCN between-group evidence is nominally significant only against the non-mucinous comparators and flips across exact tests (Barnard 0.051). ACTION: kept the pre-specified pooled test as primary but reported each type separately and added the background-rate test per type (MCN 3/8 vs background 1.1e-3 per tumour: binomial p=7.6e-8, Bonferroni x20,000 = 0.0015), which supports MCN independently of the comparator.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: Two of the three MCN RNF43 calls have weak read support: MCN_166 p.R371* has 4 alt of 15 reads and MCN_170 p.S41* has VAF 7% (14/194), the only variant in the 440-row file with VAF below 10%; the same chr17:56436026 R371* call also appears in IPMN_21 with 2 alt of 11 reads. MEANS: the MCN count could fall to 2/8 or 1/8 if these are artefacts; with 2/8 MCN vs SCA+SPN Fisher p=0.10 and background binomial p=3.4e-5 (not significant after x20,000), with 1/8 nothing is significant for MCN. IPMN (6/8, each tumour retains a well-supported call) and the pooled test (p=0.0025 to 0.0068) are unaffected. ACTION: did not filter, because the file is the study's curated somatic call set and 35 of 440 rows have fewer than 5 alt reads, so 4 alt reads is within the study's calling threshold; reported the filtered results as a sensitivity analysis and named MCN as the weakest point.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: Background non-silent mutation load differs about 9-fold by tumour type (mean per tumour: IPMN 24.9, MCN 14.1, SCA 8.5, SPN 2.9; TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS equals this count divided by 30 Mb). MEANS: a between-type comparison of any gene is partly confounded by mutation load, since IPMN/MCN have more passenger mutations than SCA/SPN. ACTION: ran the background-rate test with each type's own rate and with the highest-rate tumour in the group (IPMN p=2.3e-14, MCN p=4.2e-7 at 2.35 kb coding length); the expected passenger RNF43 hits in 16 IPMN+MCN tumours is about 0.02 against 9 observed, so load cannot explain the enrichment. Also 8 of 10 RNF43 mutations are nonsense vs 11.3% truncating among other non-silent mutations in the same tumours (binomial p=9.4e-7), a tumour-suppressor pattern.

label: RESULT
text: RESULT (bd02-team-a analyst): label True. Protein-altering RNF43 mutations occur in 6/8 IPMN and 3/8 MCN versus 0/8 SCA and 0/8 SPN; pooled IPMN+MCN vs SCA+SPN Fisher two-sided p=0.0008, exact 4x2 p=0.001; background-rate binomial p=1.5e-15 (IPMN) and 7.6e-8 (MCN), both below 0.05 after multiplying by 20,000 genes; 8/10 mutations are nonsense. All RNF43 rows in data_mutations.txt are protein-altering, so the any-row sensitivity gives identical counts. Weakest point is MCN, where two of three calls have low read support.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: Tumor purity differs by subtype (TP53-mut Predominant median 20% vs 10% in GNAS/RAS subtypes) and purity strongly predicts measured aneuploidy/FGA (rank-regression t=9); 52/273 samples have FGA exactly 0. MEANS: an unadjusted aneuploidy comparison could partly reflect copy-number detectability, not biology. ACTION: changed method to add purity-adjusted rank regression and purity-stratified Mann-Whitney tests; the TP53-subtype excess persists in every purity stratum (FGA p=6e-4, 2e-4, 0.01) and after adjustment (p=5e-7), so the conclusion holds.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: OS_MONTHS is missing for 29/273 patients, i.e. all 27 stage I-III patients plus 2 others, because OS is defined from metastasis diagnosis; 26 of them still have OS_STATUS=LIVING. MEANS: the prognosis comparison applies only to the 244 stage IV patients (84 deaths) and status without time must not be used. ACTION: restricted survival analysis to rows with both time and status; aneuploidy analysis keeps all 273. Method unchanged otherwise.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: OS clock starts at metastasis but patients enter the cohort at sequencing; entry delay (age at sequencing minus age at mets, whole-year resolution) ranges -60 to +168 months, mean 6.8, and 9 patients have delay >= OS time. MEANS: possible immortal-time/left-truncation bias in naive Kaplan-Meier/Cox. ACTION: added a left-truncated (delayed-entry) Cox model; HR for TP53-mut Predominant vs others 2.47 (1.60-3.83) versus naive 2.35 (1.53-3.62), so the result is robust; ages are whole years so the truncation correction is coarse.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: TP53-mut Predominant OS is significantly worse than GNAS-mut (log-rank p=4e-4) and RAS-mut (p=3e-5) subtypes but NOT different from Triple-Negative (median 35 vs 42 months, p=0.32); also histology is confounded with subtype (colonic-type enriched in TP53, mucinous in GNAS), and within-histology effects are significant only in mucinous (HR 3.05, p=5e-4; goblet HR 1.65, colonic HR 1.53, both n.s. but same direction). MEANS: 'poor prognosis' holds for TP53 vs the cohort as a whole and vs GNAS/RAS, not as uniquely worst subtype. ACTION: kept TP53-vs-rest as primary contrast but added histology-stratified and covariate-adjusted Cox (HR 2.13 and 2.30, p<0.001); label stays True, caveat reported.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE in the sample table is not a 0-39 arm-level count but a continuous value ranging 0 to 2.2e7 (median 7.7e5). MEANS: its definition is unclear so parametric comparisons on raw scale are unsafe and it should be cross-checked. ACTION: used rank-based tests only and corroborated with FGA (Spearman 0.91 with aneuploidy score) and with FGA recomputed from the seg file (|seg.mean|>=0.2; Spearman 0.997 with reported FGA); all three give TP53-subtype vs rest p~1e-11.

label: RESULT
text: RESULT (bd03-team-b): In the appendiceal cancer dataset (273 patients, 1 sample each), TP53-mut Predominant subtype (n=86) has higher aneuploidy score (median 2.9e6 vs 0.2-0.6e6) and FGA (0.073 vs 0.002-0.004), Mann-Whitney p~1e-11, robust to purity/histology adjustment; and worse OS among 244 stage IV patients (median 35 mo; HR vs rest 2.35, 95% CI 1.53-3.62; adjusted 2.30; left-truncated 2.47). Label chosen: True.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: Tumour purity differs by subtype (median 20% in TP53-mut Predominant vs 10% in the rest, Mann-Whitney p=5e-6; purity<=20% in 53% of TP53 vs 80-85% of GNAS/RAS) and purity correlates with every aneuploidy metric (Spearman 0.48-0.53). MEANS: part of the raw TP53-vs-rest aneuploidy gap could be a purity artefact, so the unadjusted Mann-Whitney is not sufficient alone. ACTION: added purity-adjusted rank regression (TP53 coefficient stays +0.18 to +0.23 rank units, p<=1.4e-7 on all five metrics, also after adding histology and sample type) and purity-stratified tests (purity>=20: FGA median 0.103 vs 0.011, p=4e-6; purity>=30: 0.145 vs 0.040, p=0.01; purity<20: p=3e-4); the effect survives with the same direction in every stratum.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: The survival contrast is not uniform across comparator subtypes: TP53-mut Predominant vs Triple-Negative HR=1.30 (95% CI 0.77-2.19, log-rank p=0.32), while vs GNAS HR=2.66 (1.52-4.66) and vs RAS HR=5.82 (2.28-14.9; RAS has only 5 deaths). Also OS is missing for 29 patients, exactly those not stage IV, and 11 patients have negative sequencing delay with 9 having delay>=OS (whole-year age precision). MEANS: TP53 subtype is worse than the pooled rest (HR 2.35, 1.53-3.62, p=1e-4, 39 vs 45 deaths) but shares the poor-prognosis end with Triple-Negative; survival conclusions apply to stage IV patients only. ACTION: kept the pre-specified TP53-vs-rest contrast as primary; confirmed with delayed-entry Cox (HR 2.42-2.47, p<1e-4) and multivariable Cox adjusting grade, histology, age (HR 1.93, 1.24-3.00, p=0.004); PH test p=0.12.

label: RESULT
text: RESULT (bd03-team-a): In the appendiceal cancer cohort (273 patients, one sample each), the TP53-mut Predominant subtype (n=86) has higher aneuploidy than the other subtypes pooled on all metrics (FGA median 0.073 vs 0.003; provided ANEUPLOIDY_SCORE 2.9e6 vs 3.4e5; recomputed arm fraction at |seg.mean|>0.2 0.077 vs 0; all Mann-Whitney p<1e-10, robust to purity adjustment) and worse OS (median 35 months vs not reached; HR 2.35, 95% CI 1.53-3.62; 244 patients, 84 deaths). Provided FGA is reproduced from the .seg file as length with |seg.mean|>0.2 over total length including chrX (Spearman 0.996, median abs diff 2e-5). Label chosen: True.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: the four files hold no outcome variable for RNA splicing (no expression, exon-usage or transcript table) and no direct haematopoiesis measure (no blood counts, blast percent, colony or reconstitution data); the mutation file has only 23 filled columns, with allele counts, validation and mutation status all empty. MEANS: the hypothesis outcome side cannot be tested directly; only mutation presence, recurrence and coarse clinical class (WHO class, IPSS for 13 of 29) are available. ACTION: changed the method from an effect test to (a) selection-signature tests on the mutations and (b) association with WHO/disease class as a weak phenotype proxy, and treated the label as a question of whether indirect evidence suffices.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: all 29 patients have a myeloid neoplasm (18 MDS, 7 tAML, 4 CMML) and there are no healthy or non-myeloid controls. MEANS: disease versus no-disease cannot be compared by splicing-mutation status, so 'affects haematopoiesis' cannot be tested as a case-control contrast; only within-disease subtype contrasts are possible. ACTION: restricted phenotype tests to within-cohort contrasts and reported them as underpowered.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: the disease-type association of splicing mutations moves with the gene-set definition: exact permutation p=0.019 for U2AF1/SRSF2/ZRSR2 only (CMML 4/4, MDS 8/18, tAML 1/7) but p=0.086 for the six-gene set adding SF3B1, SF3A1, PRPF40B (CMML 4/4, MDS 10/18, tAML 2/7); IPSS, age, TMB and high-blast contrasts are all p>0.1. MEANS: the within-cohort phenotype signal is not robust to a reasonable analytic choice and the three-gene set was chosen after seeing recurrence. ACTION: did not treat it as evidence of an effect on haematopoiesis; reported both numbers.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: the four tables hold no direct readout of either half of the hypothesis: no RNA/expression/isoform table (only WXS mutation calls, 260 rows) and no blood-count, blast-percentage or dysplasia column (patient columns are only SEX, AGE, WHO_CLASS, CYTOGENETICS, IPSS_SCORE). MEANS: a splicing effect cannot be measured and haematopoiesis can only be addressed indirectly through selection of mutations in a clonal haematopoietic disease and disease subtype. ACTION: changed the method from a mutant-vs-wild-type phenotype comparison to a selection test (observed vs expected hits in a pre-fixed spliceosome gene set, hotspot recurrence, mutual exclusivity); all conclusions stated as indirect.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: minor file mismatches in the MDS Tokyo-style dataset: MDS-13 has zero mutation rows (TMB 0, consistent), tAML-01 has TMB 0.5 (implies 15 at the 30 Mb denominator used by the other 28 samples) but 14 rows in data_mutations.txt, and the mutation file has no silent variants (only missense, nonsense, frameshift, splice). MEANS: one mutation is missing for tAML-01 and a synonymous background rate cannot be estimated from the file, so enrichment must use a length-based background. ACTION: kept all rows; used a CDS-length background with a 10x inflated sensitivity check (enrichment of six core splicing genes 16 of 260 mutations vs 0.12 expected, p=3e-29, and p=1e-13 at 10x background).

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: data_mutations.txt contains zero Silent variants (classes: 197 missense, 22 nonsense, 30 frameshift, 11 splice-site) and all t_ref/t_alt/n count columns, Entrez_Gene_Id, Validation_Status and Mutation_Status are empty; the Hotspot column is 0 for all 260 rows even for SF3B1 K700E and SRSF2 P95H. MEANS: a silent-vs-non-silent (dN/dS-type) comparison is impossible, allele fraction/clone size cannot be computed, and the Hotspot column is uninformative. ACTION: used a length-based Poisson expectation with a 5x mutability allowance instead of dN/dS, and defined hotspots by recurrence of Protein_position across patients; made no clonality claims.

label: Splicing mutation facts
text: In the 29-patient myelodysplasia WXS dataset, 16 of 29 patients (55 percent) carry a mutation in a splicing-machinery gene (U2AF1 5, ZRSR2 5, SRSF2 3, SF3B1 1, SF3A1 1, PRPF40B 1; plus LUC7L2 in one U2AF1 patient); hotspots are SRSF2 P95 (3 patients, two different substitutions) and U2AF1 Q157 (3, two substitutions) plus S34F; the six core genes are fully mutually exclusive (16 hits in 16 patients, permutation p=0.013); all five ZRSR2 mutations are in males (chrX). (2) Legacy format (deprecated, dropped in v5.0.0): a separate data_fusions.txt (meta genetic_alteration_type FUSION, datatype FUSION) with columns Hugo_Symbol, Entrez_Gene_Id, Center, Tumor_Sample_Barcode, Fusion, DNA_support, RNA_support, Method, Frame; on import these rows were stored as fusion-typed events inside the mutation profile/mutation table, which is why older mutation exports can contain rows with Variant_Classification 'Fusion' (the docs describe this at database level; a literal 'Fusion' row in data_mutations.txt is therefore possible in old exports but is not a documented input value: the documented MAF Variant_Classification list has no 'Fusion'). text: FINDING: No. SNV/indel callers that produce MAF rows cannot report a genomic rearrangement, so the absence of small-variant rows near a gene says nothing about rearrangements there. Small-variant callers are size-limited by design (Strelka: 'SNVs and indels up to a predefined maximum size, currently defaulting to 49 bases or less'), and the MAF Variant_Type field has only SNP, DNP, TNP, ONP, INS, DEL: there is no value for a translocation, inversion or breakend. Structural variants are conventionally events of 50 bp or more (deletions, duplications, insertions, inversions, translocations) and are found by different evidence (discordant read pairs, split reads, read depth, local assembly) using dedicated callers (Manta, Delly, Lumpy, GRIDSS, SvABA, BRASS, Pindel for the smallest), which write breakend (BND) records in VCF or BEDPE; the GDC releases these as files separate from the SNV/indel output. The only overlap is at the size boundary: SV callers such as Manta/SvABA also emit medium indels, and a sub-50-bp insertion or deletion in a gene's upstream region could appear as a 5'Flank MAF row if that region was sequenced, but that is a small indel, not a rearrangement joining distant loci. For TERT specifically, a neuroblastoma review states the rearrangements were discovered by whole-genome sequencing, that breakpoints cluster in a ~50 kb region upstream of the TERT transcription start site without affecting the gene itself, and that clinical detection is by FISH or WGS; exome/targeted capture does not cover that non-coding region, so even an SV caller run on exome data would usually miss them (this last step is inference from the capture design plus earlier department sources, not a sentence read in this session). Confidence: high for the caller/format answer, medium-high for the exome inference. QUESTION: Can small-variant calling from exome or genome sequencing (SNV/indel callers producing MAF rows) ever report a genomic rearrangement whose breakpoints lie in the non-coding region upstream of a gene, or are such events only reported by dedicated structural-variant callers and stored separately?
